text:
OncallBot: INCIDENT ALERT — embeddings-service (us-west1) elevated error rate and partial degradation detected. 5xx% jumped to ~18% over last 5m; a cluster of "dimension_mismatch" and OOM/503s. Auto-page sent.
Mia: I'll take this one, pinging infra and ml.
Devin: any deploys in the last 30m? I don't see active CI merges but autoscaler bumped workers at ~1773000900.
Raj: seeing a pattern: several clients that were migrated to model `embed-xlarge-1536` are still sending 1024-d vectors for batch-upsert/rerank. The runtime throws a vector size check deeper in the pipeline and ends up returning 500 instead of a clean 400.
Sophia: that explains dimension_mismatch. Do we normalize/validate at the edge? Should have earlier.
Mia: grabbing logs. key error snippet:
```
ERROR runtime embeddings/serve.go:215 vector size mismatch: expected=1536 got=1024 tenant=cust_42 req_id=8f3a2a
stack: embeddings/serve.go:215 -> pipeline/batch.go:88 -> http/handler.go:43
metric: response_code=500
```
Mia: also seeing burst of `batch_runner` CPU and a few OOM kill restarts on worker-3 around 1773001102.
Kelly: SupportEngine forwarded one repro payload from customer: they call our upsert with precomputed vectors shaped to 1024 because they upgraded client lib incorrectly.
SupportEngine: copied example payload (redacted):
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "embed-xlarge-1536",
  "input": ["..."],
  "vector": [ /* 1024 numbers */ ]
}
```
SupportEngine: in their SDK, default vector_dim was 1024, they thought server would auto-pad.
Raj: trying a local repro now. curl to staging reproduces 500 and the same stacktrace. curl snippet:
```
curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxx' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"embed-xlarge-1536","input":["hello"],"vector":[0,0,...(1024 entries)...]}'
```
Devin: immediate mitigation options: 1) route cust_42 to `embed-compat-1024` (drop-in 1024-d model) 2) add edge-level validation to return 400 for vector-dimension mismatch (safer than 500) 3) temporarily disable large batch coalescing for embedding endpoints to reduce OOM pressure.
Mia: I can push a routing override for that tenant to the canary pool. Doing it now: `redwoodctl routes patch tenant=cust_42 --model embed-compat-1024 --scope=canary`
Mia: pushed. Waiting for traffic shift.
OncallBot: ROUTE CHANGE applied to canary nodes. 10% traffic diversion in progress.
Raj: after diversion, errors for cust_42 dropped to 1.2% and cluster CPU returned to baseline. The global 5xx rate fell to ~3.4%. Nice.
Sophia: still want to harden: we need preflight validation that rejects mismatched vectors with 400 and a clear error message. Also add a metric for "vector_dim_mismatch_count" that triggers Pager if > 5/min for any tenant.
Kelly: customer-facing action: SupportEngine drafted a message for cust_42 explaining root cause and mitigation steps (client lib upgrade + server fallback). Want approval before sending. Quick ack?
Devin: +1 on message, emphasize workaround and ETA for permanent fix.
Mia: remaining work items:
- infra: create alert on vector_dim_mismatch_count (>5/min) and move from warning to P1 for tenant impact.
- runtime: return 400 at edge for dimension mismatch, avoid internal 500.
- batching: default to smaller `max_batch_size` for embedding endpoints and add per-tenant overrides.
- ml: publish an `embed-compat-1024` alias for problematic migrations.
Raj: I'll own runtime change (edge validation). Putting up PR for `edge-validate` now, will add tests for 1024/1536 cases.
Sophia: I'll add new metric and adjust alert thresholds in observability.
Mia: SupportEngine, please send the customer note after Kelly reviews.
SupportEngine: draft ready, sending in 10m.
OncallBot: UPDATE — after routing change at 1773001700, system error rate stabilized. Severity degraded to SEV-3.
Mia: marking incident as mitigated; leaving thread open until PRs land and customer notified.
Devin: followup: full postmortem and timeline to be posted to #postmortems once we close actions.
Kelly: customer confirmed they received note and rolled client update. They reported reduced errors after client update at ~1773002100.
Mia: closing oncall handoff. Final state: routing override active, customer updated, PR for edge validation in review, alert created.
OncallBot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (partial) — ticketing: INC-1773001234.
Mia: thanks team, good catch. We should add a small runbook step for embedding migrations.
